title: Angles: lines, parallels and triangles
hook: A straight line is $180^{\circ}$, a triangle is $180^{\circ}$, and parallel lines copy angles.

steps.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is $130^{\circ}$. The two interior angles not next to it add to:
steps.why: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

steps.prompt: From memory: what do the angles in a triangle add up to?
Two angles of a triangle are $47^{\circ}$ and $68^{\circ}$. Find the third.
Two angles form a straight line. One is $115^{\circ}$. The other is:
Match each pair or set of angles to its rule.
steps.why: Vertical angles are equal. A straight line is $180^{\circ}$, a full turn is $360^{\circ}$, and complementary means $90^{\circ}$.

steps.prompt: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is $72^{\circ}$. Its alternate interior angle is:
Same lines: the same-side interior angle to that $72^{\circ}$ angle is:
An isosceles triangle has a $40^{\circ}$ top angle. Finding a base angle. Tap the line with the mistake.

keys: Straight line: $180^{\circ}$. Triangle: $180^{\circ}$. Around a point: $360^{\circ}$.
Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
Isosceles: the base angles are equal.

recall.prompt: A triangle has angles of $90^{\circ}$ and $35^{\circ}$. What is the third angle?

recall.why: Opposite angles at a crossing are equal.
